title: Add FieldComment and FieldIssueReport Prisma models
description:
Field currently has lat/lng but no way for users to comment on it or report physical defects (potholes, broken lighting, etc.). Note: FieldReport already exists (server/prisma/schema.prisma:84) but is a completely different feature (crowdsourced busy-level polling) -- do not reuse or rename it, add new models alongside it.

Add:
```
model FieldComment {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  fieldId   String
  userId    String
  text      String
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  field     Field    @relation(fields: [fieldId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  user      User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([fieldId, createdAt])
}

enum FieldIssueCategory {
  POTHOLE
  LIGHTING
  SURFACE
  GOAL_NET
  FENCE
  OTHER
}

enum FieldIssueStatus {
  OPEN
  RESOLVED
}

model FieldIssueReport {
  id          String             @id @default(cuid())
  fieldId     String
  userId      String
  category    FieldIssueCategory
  description String?
  status      FieldIssueStatus   @default(OPEN)
  createdAt   DateTime           @default(now())
  resolvedAt  DateTime?
  field       Field              @relation(fields: [fieldId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  user        User               @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([fieldId, status])
  @@index([fieldId, createdAt])
}
```
On `model Field` (server/prisma/schema.prisma:48-78) add relation arrays `comments FieldComment[]` and `issueReports FieldIssueReport[]` next to the existing `reports FieldReport[]` (line 72). On `model User` add matching back-relation arrays `fieldComments FieldComment[]` and `fieldIssueReports FieldIssueReport[]` (Prisma requires both sides declared), following the existing array-field style already used on User (e.g. `ratingsGiven`, `notifications`).

After editing the schema, run `npx prisma migrate dev --name add_field_comments_and_issue_reports` from `server/` (needs `directUrl`, see .cursor/rules/prisma-db.mdc) and `npx prisma generate` so the client matches immediately (stale-client pitfall documented in prisma-db.mdc).

title: Add comment and issue-report endpoints to fields.js
description:
Add six routes to server/routes/fields.js, following the file's existing conventions (mapFieldForClient-style plain response shaping, authenticateToken/requireAdmin already imported at lines 97-98):

1. `GET /:id/comments` -- public, no auth. `prisma.fieldComment.findMany({ where: { fieldId }, orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' }, take/skip like the pattern in GET '/' (lines 132-146), include: { user: { select: { id: true, name: true, imageUrl: true } } } })`. Map to `{ id, text, createdAt, user: { id, name, imageUrl } }`.
2. `POST /:id/comments` -- `authenticateToken`. Body `{ text }`; validate non-empty, trim, max 1000 chars (400 if invalid). Verify field exists (404 otherwise, same pattern as POST /:id/report at line 419). Create with `userId: req.user.id`. Return 201 with the created comment (same shape as #1, including the current user's name/imageUrl from req.user or a fresh lookup).
3. `DELETE /:id/comments/:commentId` -- `authenticateToken`. Load the comment, 404 if missing/wrong fieldId. Allow delete only if `comment.userId === req.user.id || req.user.isAdmin` (403 otherwise, mirrors auth invariant in .cursor/rules/server-invariants.mdc "never trust a client-supplied userId"). Delete and return `{ message: 'Comment deleted' }`.
4. `GET /:id/issues` -- public. `prisma.fieldIssueReport.findMany({ where: { fieldId }, orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' } })`. Map to `{ id, category, description, status, createdAt }` -- deliberately omit `userId` from the public list (no reporter identity leak, same spirit as the friends-only game exclusion in GET /:id/analytics at line 341).
5. `POST /:id/issues` -- `authenticateToken`. Body `{ category, description }`; validate `category` is one of POTHOLE/LIGHTING/SURFACE/GOAL_NET/FENCE/OTHER (400 otherwise), `description` optional string capped at 1000 chars. Verify field exists (404). Create with `userId: req.user.id`, `status: 'OPEN'`. Return 201 with `{ id, category, description, status, createdAt }`.
6. `PATCH /:id/issues/:issueId` -- `authenticateToken`, `requireAdmin`. Body `{ status }`, must be OPEN or RESOLVED. Update the issue (also set `resolvedAt: new Date()` when transitioning to RESOLVED, `resolvedAt: null` when reopened). Return the updated issue.

Place all six after the existing POST /:id/report handler (~line 444) and before `// Get field by ID` (line 447), so field-scoped read/write routes stay grouped.

title: Web API client: comments/issues methods on fieldsApi
Field page (web): location map, comments, issue reports
description:
1. Create `next_app/src/components/FieldCommentsSection.tsx` ("use client"): props `{ fieldId: string }`. On mount, `fieldsApi.getComments(fieldId)` and render a list (avatar via existing `Avatar` component pattern, name, relative/absolute time via `formatJerusalemDate`/`formatJerusalemTime` from `@/utils/timezone` -- never a bare `toLocaleString()`, see server/docs/agents/frontend_rules.md section 2.1). Below the list, a signed-in-only text field + submit button (use `useAuth()` from `@clerk/nextjs` for the token, same pattern as `CrowdReportWidget.tsx`); on submit call `fieldsApi.addComment`, prepend the returned comment to local state (optimistic-friendly: append after success, no need for tempId reconciliation since this list isn't fed by sockets). Show a sign-in prompt (no form) when signed out, matching the `!userId` Alert pattern already on the field page (next_app/src/app/fields/[id]/page.tsx:166-170).

2. Create `next_app/src/components/FieldIssueReportSection.tsx` ("use client"): props `{ fieldId: string }`. On mount, `fieldsApi.getIssues(fieldId)` and render existing OPEN issues as a small chip/list (category label in Hebrew: בור, תאורה לקויה, משטח פגום, שער/רשת פגומים, גדר פגומה, אחר) so users can see what's already reported before submitting a duplicate. Below it, a signed-in-only form: category `<select>`/MUI `Select` + optional free-text description + submit; on submit call `fieldsApi.addIssue`, show a success confirmation (mirror `CrowdReportWidget`'s Snackbar pattern), and prepend the new issue to the local OPEN list.

3. In `next_app/src/app/fields/[id]/page.tsx`: add `lat?: number | null; lng?: number | null;` to the local `Field` type (currently missing, lines 20-36 -- the API already returns these two columns via `mapFieldForClient`'s spread in server/routes/fields.js, they're just not typed here). Import `GameLocationMap` from `@/components/GameLocationMap` (already a "use client" component; it's rendered directly inside a Server Component today via GameActions.tsx with no `dynamic(ssr:false)` wrapper needed -- despite server/docs/agents/frontend_rules.md section 1.1 listing it as "Leaflet-based", the actual source (next_app/src/components/GameLocationMap.tsx) uses `@vis.gl/react-google-maps`, not Leaflet, so the existing no-dynamic-import usage in GameActions.tsx is the correct precedent to copy, not the doc). Render `<GameLocationMap lat={field.lat} lng={field.lng} title={field.name} height={280} />` inside a new `Card` when `typeof field.lat === 'number' && typeof field.lng === 'number'`, placed after the header Card (after line 164) and before the sign-in Alert. Then render `<FieldCommentsSection fieldId={field.id} />` and `<FieldIssueReportSection fieldId={field.id} />` after the analytics cards (after line 191), before the sticky `CrowdReportWidget` (line 194) so the sticky widget stays visually last/bottom.

title: Field screen (mobile): location map, comments, issue reports
description:
1. Create `mobile_app/src/components/FieldCommentsSection.tsx`: RN component, props `{ fieldId: string }`. Fetch via `fieldsApi.getComments` on mount, render a list (name + relative time), and a signed-in-only `TextInput` + submit `TouchableOpacity` (use `useAuth()` from `@clerk/clerk-expo` for the token, matching the auth pattern already used in `mobile_app/app/field/[id].tsx`). Match this codebase's existing RN styling convention in that screen (NativeWind `className` utility classes, not StyleSheet -- see `FieldProfileHeader` for the pattern).

2. Create `mobile_app/src/components/FieldIssueReportSection.tsx`: RN component, props `{ fieldId: string }`. Fetch via `fieldsApi.getIssues`, render existing OPEN issues (Hebrew category labels, same mapping as web step 4), and a signed-in-only category picker (a simple row of selectable chips is fine, RN has no native `<select>`) + optional description `TextInput` + submit. On success show a brief inline confirmation state (mirror the `reportState: 'idle'|'submitting'|'done'` pattern already declared in this screen at field/[id].tsx line ~51 for the crowd-report widget).

3. In `mobile_app/app/field/[id].tsx`: the `Field` interface (mobile_app/src/services/api/fields.ts) already includes `lat`/`lng` -- no type change needed here. Add a `MapView` (from `react-native-maps`, already a dependency and already used identically in `mobile_app/app/game/[id].tsx` lines 2, 338-355) rendered when `field?.lat` and `field?.lng` are both numbers, with a single `Marker` at that position and `title={field.name}`. Place it after the header/image section and before the busy-times chart section. Then render `<FieldCommentsSection fieldId={fieldId} />` and `<FieldIssueReportSection fieldId={fieldId} />` after the existing analytics/schedule sections.

title: Team-management page (web): show field location map
description:
The web "team page" is next_app/src/app/games/[id]/team-management/page.tsx, which renders `LiveTeamManagement` (next_app/src/components/LiveTeamManagement.tsx). It fetches live pick-session state via `gamesApi.getPickSession` (next_app/src/services/api/games.ts:106-108), which hits `GET /api/games/:id/pick-session`. That endpoint's server-side builder (server/services/pickSessionService.js:303-321) already returns `game: mapGameForClient(game, viewerId)` -- which already includes `fieldLat`/`fieldLng`/`fieldName` (server/services/gameService.js:152-164/255-258) -- but the client-side `PickSessionState` type (next_app/src/services/api/games.ts:28-59) doesn't declare a `game` field at all, so it's currently inaccessible in a type-safe way. No server change is needed here, only typing + rendering.

1. In `next_app/src/services/api/games.ts`, add to the `PickSessionState` type: `game?: { fieldName?: string | null; fieldLat?: number | null; fieldLng?: number | null } | null;`.
2. In `next_app/src/components/LiveTeamManagement.tsx`, import `GameLocationMap` from `@/components/GameLocationMap` and render it (in a small Card, near the top of the page, above or alongside the pick-status header) when `state?.game?.fieldLat`/`fieldLng` are both numbers, passing `title={state.game.fieldName}`.

title: Team-management screen (mobile): show field location map
description:
The mobile "team page" is mobile_app/app/game/teams/[id].tsx (same live pick-session feature as web step 7, via `gamesApi.getPickSession` at mobile_app/src/services/api/games.ts:186-188, typed `any` there so no client-side type change is needed for that call). The screen's local `PickState` type (lines 15-40) doesn't declare a `game` field even though the server response already includes one (see step 7's server-side explanation) -- `setState(data)` at line 105 stores the raw response as-is, so `state.game` is already present at runtime.

1. Add `game?: { fieldName?: string | null; fieldLat?: number | null; fieldLng?: number | null } | null;` to the `PickState` type (lines 15-40).
2. Import `MapView, { Marker }` from `react-native-maps` (already used identically in mobile_app/app/game/[id].tsx lines 2, 338-355) and render a small map (with one `Marker`) near the top of the screen when `state?.game?.fieldLat`/`fieldLng` are both numbers, using `state.game.fieldName` as the marker title.

title: Fix stale participants/chat after join/leave on web game page
description:
Unrelated bug fix (reported separately, not part of the map/comments feature above): on the web game page, joining or leaving a game updates the header/join-button instantly but the participants list and the chat panel stay stale until a manual reload.

Root cause (confirmed by investigation): `next_app/src/app/games/[id]/page.tsx` is an async Server Component. It computes `joined` once at SSR time (line 97: `const joined = !!userId && (game?.participants || []).some((p) => p.id === userId);`) and uses it to gate the Chat card (lines 251-280) and `GameRatingsPanel` (line 245), and it passes the static SSR `game.participants` straight into `TeamBuilderWrapper` (line 229) -> `GameParticipantsList` (which reads the `participants` prop directly, no local copy -- next_app/src/components/GameParticipantsList.tsx:82,97). Meanwhile `GameLiveSection.tsx` already owns a live, socket-and-merge-updated copy of `game` (including `participants`) entirely internally (`mergeAndSet` at line 97-99, `game:updated` socket listener at lines 84-95, `joined` recomputed live at line 129) -- but nothing outside `GameLiveSection` can see that live state, because `page.tsx` can't hold client state (it's a Server Component) and can't pass functions/render-props across the server/client boundary to read it back out.

Fix: make `GameLiveSection` the single live-state owner for the whole participants+chat+ratings section, not just the header/button, by moving `TeamBuilderWrapper`, `GameRatingsPanel`, and the Chat `Card` block into it so they read from its internal live `game` state instead of page.tsx's static props.

1. In `next_app/src/components/GameLiveSection.tsx`:
   - Add to the `LiveGame` type: `organizerId: string; chatRoomId?: string; overbooked?: boolean; lotteryAt?: string | null; managers?: { id: string; name?: string; avatar?: string; role?: string }[]; teams?: { id: string; name: string; color: string; playerIds: string[] }[]; waitlistParticipants?: Participant[]; pickSessionStatus?: string | null;` (these need to travel with the live `game` state since they're now read from it, not from separate props -- note `initialGame` already gets merged wholesale via `setGame((prev) => ({ ...prev, ...initialGame }))` at line 63 and via `normalizeIncomingGame` merges, so once they're part of `LiveGame` they'll flow through the existing merge logic unchanged).
   - Add a new prop `currentUserId: string` (page.tsx already has this as `userId`; `viewerId` prop is the same value today -- reuse `viewerId` instead of adding a duplicate, don't introduce two names for the same id).
   - Import `TeamBuilderWrapper` from `@/components/TeamBuilderWrapper`, `GameRatingsPanel` from `@/components/GameRatingsPanel`, `Chat` from `@/components/Chat`, plus `Grid` from `@mui/material/Grid` and `Card`/`Typography` (Typography already imported).
   - After the existing `<GameHeaderCard>...</GameHeaderCard>` and the `canManageSeries && <PendingJoinRequests .../>` block (current end of the component, line ~265), add the `<Grid container>` block moved from page.tsx (current lines 223-281 there): left column renders `<TeamBuilderWrapper gameId={game.id} participants={game.participants} organizerId={game.organizerId} initialManagers={game.managers || []} maxPlayers={game.maxPlayers} currentUserId={viewerId} initialTeams={game.teams || []} lotteryData={{ enabled: !!game.lotteryEnabled, pending: !!game.lotteryPending, overbooked: !!game.overbooked, at: game.lotteryAt || null, signups: game.totalSignups || 0 }} waitlistParticipants={game.waitlistParticipants || []} pickSessionStatus={game.pickSessionStatus || null} />` then `{joined && <GameRatingsPanel gameId={game.id} />}` (reuse the `joined` already computed at line 129); right column renders the same Chat `Card` markup currently in page.tsx (lines 252-279), gated on the *live* `joined`, using `roomId={game.chatRoomId || game.id}` and `chatName={game.title || "Game Chat"}`.

2. In `next_app/src/app/games/[id]/page.tsx`:
   - Add `organizerId: game.organizerId, chatRoomId: game.chatRoomId, overbooked: game.overbooked, lotteryAt: game.lotteryAt, managers: game.managers, teams: game.teams, waitlistParticipants: game.waitlistParticipants, pickSessionStatus: (game as { pickSessionStatus?: string }).pickSessionStatus` into the `initialGame={{ ... }}` object passed to `GameLiveSection` (lines 122-143).
   - Delete the now-unused `const joined = ...` line (97) -- confirm nothing else in this file reads `joined` first (only the two removed usages at lines 245 and 251 in the current version).
   - Delete the entire `<Grid container>...</Grid>` block (lines 223-281) since it now lives inside `GameLiveSection`.
   - Remove the now-unused imports this leaves behind in this file: `Chat`, `TeamBuilderWrapper`, `GameRatingsPanel`, `Grid`, and `Card`/`Typography` if (and only if) nothing else in the file still uses them -- double check each before deleting, since e.g. `Divider`/`Box` are still used elsewhere in the file.
   - Leave `GameActions`, `GameDetailsEditor`, `SeriesManager`, and the field-profile link untouched (lines 148-219) -- they're independent of this bug.

After this change, verify manually (dev server, two browser sessions or one session + incognito) that: (a) joining as the acting user immediately shows them in the participants list and opens the chat panel without a reload, (b) leaving immediately removes them from participants and closes the chat panel without a reload, (c) an already-open second viewer's page still updates live via the existing `game:updated` socket broadcast now that the listener's target state also drives participants/chat, not just the header.

Known separate, smaller gap surfaced by the same investigation (do NOT fix as part of this step -- flag only): `broadcastGameUpdate` in `server/services/gameService.js` (lines 428-448) only sends `game:updated` to the organizer, current participants, and roles -- a user who has the game page open without having joined/managed it will not see a live update when someone else joins or leaves. That's a distinct feature gap (live updates for idle spectators), not the reported bug (which is about the acting user's own join/leave), so it's out of scope here unless the user asks for it separately.
